_doc: Major temples by deity, for the Temples screen. 'site' and 'donate' are only ever a temple's own official address, checked on 2026-10-21 and, for the temples in Nepal, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and the diaspora countries, 2026-10-22 (government .gov.in/.nic.in portals, the temple board's own domain, or a domain the temple's Wikipedia entry and official notices name). Several look-alike domains were found serving spam, so nothing is added from a guess: a temple whose official address could not be confirmed has neither, and the app says offerings are made at the temple; one whose site has no donation page of its own has the site only. Descriptions say why a temple is significant and famous; no remedies, papam or fear framing (content/scripts/audit_content.py). English for now; native text to follow with review.

temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple
temples.about: On the seventh of the Tirumala hills stands Lord Venkateswara, Vishnu as he came to dwell in the Kali Yuga. It is among the most visited places of worship in the world, famous for its laddu prasadam, for devotees offering their hair in gratitude, and for the Brahmotsavam each autumn.
tips: Darshan slots and rooms are booked on the TTD website; the walk up from Alipiri takes three to four hours.

temples.name: Guruvayur Sri Krishna Temple
temples.about: Guruvayurappan, Krishna as a child holding the conch, discus, mace and lotus, is said to have been installed by Guru and Vayu, which gives the town its name. Called the Dwaraka of the South, it is famous for its many first-rice ceremonies and weddings, its temple elephants, and the Guruvayur Ekadasi.
tips: Men wear mundu without a shirt; women saree or churidar. Phones and cameras are left at the counters outside.

temples.name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
temples.about: Vishnu reclines on the serpent Ananta in an image so large it is seen through three doors: the face, the navel with Brahma on the lotus, and the feet. One of the 108 Divya Desams, it gave Thiruvananthapuram its name and is known for its Dravidian gopuram and its Alpashy and Painkuni festivals.
tips: A strict dress code: men in mundu without a shirt, women in saree or a mundu over other clothes; phones are not allowed inside.

temples.name: Badrinath Temple
temples.about: High in the Garhwal Himalaya beside the Alaknanda, Badrinarayan is Vishnu in meditation. One of the four Char Dham and among the 108 Divya Desams, it is open from spring to the onset of winter, when the deity is taken down to Joshimath.
tips: Open from about May to November; Char Dham registration is required.

temples.name: Shri Vitthal Rukmini Mandir
temples.about: Vitthal, Krishna standing on a brick with hands on his hips, waiting for his devotee Pundalik, is the heart of Maharashtra's Varkari tradition. Every Ashadhi Ekadashi the wari, lakhs of pilgrims walking from Alandi and Dehu singing the abhangas of Dnyaneshwar and Tukaram, arrives here.

temples.name: Shree Jagannath Temple
temples.about: Jagannath, Lord of the Universe, with Balabhadra and Subhadra, is worshipped in wooden forms renewed in the Nabakalebara ceremony. One of the Char Dham, it is famous for the Rath Yatra, when the three ride out on giant chariots, and for the Mahaprasad cooked in its vast kitchen.
tips: Only Hindus are admitted inside the temple; the Rath Yatra in Ashadha is open to all on the streets.

temples.name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple
temples.about: On an island in the Kaveri, Ranganatha reclines on Adisesha. The first of the 108 Divya Desams and among the largest functioning temple complexes in the world, with seven enclosures and the towering Rajagopuram, it celebrates Vaikunta Ekadasi on a grand scale.

temples.name: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple
temples.about: Vishwanath, Lord of the Universe, is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, on the western bank of the Ganga in Kashi, held to be among the oldest living cities. The gilded spire and the Kashi Vishwanath Dham corridor down to the ghats draw pilgrims all year, above all on Maha Shivaratri and in Shravan.
tips: Sugam darshan and aarti tickets can be booked online; phones are not allowed inside.

temples.name: Shree Somnath Jyotirlinga
temples.about: Counted first among the twelve Jyotirlingas, Somnath stands on the Saurashtra coast where the Moon is said to have worshipped Shiva. Rebuilt many times through its history and restored in 1951, it is known for its sea-facing setting and evening light and sound show.

temples.name: Shri Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga
temples.about: The south-facing Jyotirlinga of Mahakal, Shiva as lord of time, stands in the ancient city of Ujjain. It is famous for the Bhasma Aarti before dawn and for the Simhastha Kumbh Mela held on the Shipra every twelve years.
air: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar International Airport

temples.name: Kedarnath Temple
temples.about: The highest of the Jyotirlingas, Kedarnath stands at the head of the Mandakini valley, reached on foot from Gaurikund. One of the Char Dham and the Panch Kedar, its stone temple has withstood centuries of Himalayan winters; it opens in spring and closes after Diwali.
tips: Open from about May to November; Char Dham registration is required.
A 16 km trek from Gaurikund, with ponies, palanquins and helicopters.

temples.name: Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
temples.about: In the Nallamala hills above the Krishna, Mallikarjuna is both a Jyotirlinga and, with Goddess Bhramaramba, one of the Shakti Peethas, a rare meeting of the two. It is known for its fortified walls carved with scenes from the epics and for its Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam.
tips: The temple is in the Nallamala forest; the ghat road is closed to private vehicles at night.

temples.name: Shri Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga
temples.about: Near the source of the Godavari in the Brahmagiri hills, Trimbakeshwar's Jyotirlinga has three small faces representing Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. Its black-stone temple was built in the eighteenth century, and Nashik-Trimbak hosts the Kumbh Mela every twelve years.

temples.name: Arulmigu Ramanathaswamy Temple
temples.about: On Pamban island, Ramanathaswamy is the Jyotirlinga where Rama is said to have worshipped Shiva before crossing to Lanka. One of the Char Dham, it is famous for the longest temple corridors in India and for the 22 theerthams, wells in which pilgrims bathe.

temples.name: Shri Mata Vaishno Devi
temples.about: In a cave on the Trikuta hills the Goddess is worshipped as three natural rock forms, the pindis of Mahakali, Mahalakshmi and Mahasaraswati. Millions make the twelve-kilometre climb from Katra each year, many through the night, calling 'Jai Mata Di'.
tips: A yatra registration slip is needed; the 12 km path from Katra can be walked, or ridden by pony, or shortened by helicopter to Sanjichhat.

temples.name: Maa Kamakhya Temple
temples.about: On Nilachal hill above the Brahmaputra, Kamakhya is among the most revered of the Shakti Peethas, where the Goddess is worshipped without an image, in a natural stone yoni within the sanctum. It is the centre of the Shakta tradition and famous for the Ambubachi Mela each June.
tips: The temple closes for the Ambubachi Mela in June, and the queues are longest just after.

temples.name: Arulmigu Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple
temples.about: Meenakshi, the fish-eyed Goddess and queen of Madurai, with Sundareswarar, Shiva, stands at the centre of the city. Its fourteen gopurams covered in painted figures, the Hall of a Thousand Pillars and the Chithirai festival, re-enacting their celestial wedding, make it one of Tamil Nadu's great temples.
tips: Phones are left at the entrance; the night palliyarai ceremony is worth staying for.

temples.name: Attukal Bhagavathy Temple
temples.about: Attukal Amma, identified with Kannaki of the Silappatikaram, is worshipped as a mother who protects. The Attukal Pongala each Kumbham sees lakhs of women cook pongala in the open across the city, recorded as one of the largest gatherings of women in the world.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam
temples.about: On Indrakeeladri hill above the Krishna, Kanaka Durga is believed to have appeared on her own. The Dasara Navaratri here, with the Goddess adorned in a different alankaram each day and the Teppotsavam on the river, is among the biggest in the Telugu states.

temples.name: Shri Mahalaxmi (Ambabai) Temple
temples.about: Ambabai, Mahalakshmi of Kolhapur, is one of the Shakti Peethas and the presiding goddess of the city. The temple is known for the Kiranotsav, days in the year when the setting sun's rays reach the deity's face, and for its Navaratri.

temples.name: Sri Sharadamba Temple, Sringeri
temples.about: On the Tunga river, Sharadamba, Saraswati, presides over the first of the maths founded by Adi Shankaracharya. Families come for Aksharabhyasa, a child's first letters, especially at Navaratri, and the Vidyashankara temple's zodiac pillars catch the sun month by month.

temples.name: Shree Siddhivinayak Ganapati Mandir
temples.about: Siddhivinayak, a right-trunked Ganapati with Riddhi and Siddhi, has been worshipped at Prabhadevi since 1801. Mumbai's best-loved temple, it draws long queues on Tuesdays and on Angarki Sankashti Chaturthi, and from people of every walk of life before a new beginning.
tips: Tuesdays are the busiest day; arrive early or use the temple's online darshan booking.

temples.name: Shrimant Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati
temples.about: Founded in the 1890s by the sweet-maker Dagdusheth Gadve, this Ganapati is at the centre of Pune's Ganeshotsav, the public festival Lokmanya Tilak popularised. Its richly adorned idol, themed pandals and the trust's social work are known across Maharashtra.

temples.name: Sri Varasiddhi Vinayaka Swamy Temple
temples.about: The self-manifested Vinayaka of Kanipakam is said to have emerged from a well and to keep growing. Rebuilt by the Chola king Kulothunga I, the temple is known for its Brahmotsavam beginning on Vinayaka Chavithi and for promises made before the deity.

temples.name: Karpaga Vinayagar Temple
temples.about: A rock-cut Karpaga Vinayagar with two arms and a right-curving trunk, carved in the cave temple by early Pandya craftsmen, is among the oldest images of Ganesha in Tamil Nadu. The ten-day Vinayagar Chathurthi festival ends with a giant modakam offered to him.

temples.name: Arulmigu Dhandayuthapani Swamy Temple
temples.about: On a hill above Palani, Murugan stands as Dhandayuthapani, the renunciant with a staff, in an image said to be made of navapashanam by the siddha Bogar. One of the six Arupadai Veedu, it is famous for the panchamritam prasadam and for Thai Poosam, when pilgrims walk from far away carrying kavadi.
tips: A winch and ropeway run up the hill beside the 693 steps.

temples.name: Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple
temples.about: The only one of the six Arupadai Veedu by the sea, Tiruchendur is where Murugan is said to have overcome Surapadman. The Kandha Sashti festival culminating in the Soorasamharam on the shore draws great crowds each year.

temples.name: Kukke Shree Subrahmanya Temple
temples.about: In the forests of the Western Ghats beside the Kumaradhara, Subrahmanya is worshipped as lord of the serpents, with Vasuki. The temple is known for its Champa Shashti festival in Margashira and as one of the most visited temples in Karnataka.

temples.name: Arulmigu Swaminatha Swamy Temple
temples.about: One of the six Arupadai Veedu, Swamimalai is where the child Murugan is said to have explained the meaning of Om to his father Shiva, earning the name Swaminatha, teacher of his father. Sixty steps, one for each year of the cycle, lead up to the shrine.

temples.name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Mandir
temples.about: Founded by the poet-saint Tulsidas, author of the Ramcharitmanas, Sankat Mochan, the remover of difficulties, faces Rama in the same temple. Tuesdays and Saturdays bring long queues, and the Sankat Mochan Sangeet Samaroh each April is one of India's great classical music festivals.

temples.name: Salasar Balaji Temple
temples.about: In Churu district, Salasar Balaji is Hanuman with a round, bearded and moustached face, an image said to have been found by a farmer while ploughing in 1754. Large fairs gather here at Chaitra and Ashvin Purnima.

temples.name: Hanuman Garhi
temples.about: Seventy-six steps climb to this fortress-like temple in Ayodhya, where Hanuman is said to keep watch over Rama's city. Pilgrims traditionally visit Hanuman Garhi before the Ram Janmabhoomi temple.

temples.name: Arulmigu Anjaneyar Temple
temples.about: An eighteen-foot Anjaneyar stands in the open, under the sky, facing Narasimha's cave temple across the way. Famous for the vadai malai, a garland of thousands of vadai, and the butter alankaram, it celebrates Hanumath Jayanthi in Margazhi.

temples.name: Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
temples.about: In the Periyar forests, Ayyappa, Dharma Sastha, sits in yogic posture on a hilltop reached by a forest climb. Pilgrims keep a 41-day vratham, wear black, and carry the irumudi up the eighteen holy steps, calling 'Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa'. The Mandala season and Makaravilakku draw millions.
tips: Open for the Mandala–Makaravilakku season (mid-November to mid-January) and the first days of each Malayalam month.
Pilgrims traditionally keep a 41-day vratham and carry the irumudi; book the virtual queue online before going.
Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Aryankavu Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
temples.about: One of the five Sastha temples associated with Ayyappa's life, on the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border, Aryankavu worships Sastha as a young householder. The Thrikkalyanam festival in Dhanu, his celestial wedding, is kept with Saurashtra Brahmin custom.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Shri Shaneshwar Devasthan
temples.about: Shani is worshipped here as a five-and-a-half-foot black stone in the open, without a roof. The village is famous for homes built without doors, a mark of its trust in Shani, and devotees pour oil over the stone, especially on Saturdays and Shani Amavasya.
tips: Famous for houses without doors; the temple's open-air shrine has no roof.

temples.name: Sri Dharbaranyeswarar Temple
temples.about: In this Shiva temple near Karaikal, Shani Bhagavan has his own shrine, and it is the Navagraha temple for Saturn. Pilgrims bathe in the Nala Theertham, and the temple is busiest at Sani Peyarchi, when Saturn moves into a new sign.

temples.name: Pashupatinath Temple
temples.about: On the banks of the Bagmati, Pashupatinath is Shiva as Lord of all beings and the most sacred temple of Nepal. Its pagoda with gilded roofs and silver doors stands amid hundreds of shrines and ashrams, and on Maha Shivaratri sadhus and pilgrims from across Nepal and India fill its grounds. A UNESCO World Heritage site.

temples.name: Muktinath Temple
temples.about: High in the Mustang valley at about 3,700 metres, Muktinath is one of the 108 Divya Desams sung by the Alvars, sacred to Vishnu and also to Buddhists. Pilgrims bathe under its 108 water spouts and see the eternal flame burning over water at the nearby Jwala Mai shrine; the Kali Gandaki below gives the shaligram stones.

temples.name: Janaki Mandir
temples.about: Janakpur is held to be the city of King Janaka, where Sita was born and married Rama. The white marble Janaki Mandir, built in 1910 in Mughal and Rajput style, is the heart of Vivaha Panchami, when the wedding of Sita and Rama is celebrated, and of Ram Navami in the Mithila region.

temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple
temples.about: Consecrated in 1977, among the first traditional Hindu temples built in the United States, with sculptors brought from India and the design modelled on Tirumala. It is a place of pilgrimage for Hindus across North America, known for its Venkateswara kalyanam and its annual Brahmotsavam.

temples.name: Sri Maha Vallabha Ganapati Devasthanam
temples.about: The Hindu Temple Society of North America's Ganesha temple, consecrated in 1977, is one of the oldest traditional temples in the United States. Built in granite in the South Indian style, it is famous for its Ganesha Chaturthi festival and the canteen beneath it, which serves South Indian food to visitors.

temples.name: Malibu Hindu Temple (Sri Venkateswara Swamy)
temples.about: Set in the Santa Monica Mountains and consecrated in 1981, the temple of Sri Venkateswara is the oldest Hindu temple in Southern California. Built in the Chola and Pallava style, it draws devotees from across Los Angeles for its weekend abhishekam and its Brahmotsavam.

temples.name: Shiva-Vishnu Temple
temples.about: The Hindu Community and Cultural Center's temple joins North and South Indian architecture, with Shiva and Vishnu as the principal deities and shrines for many others. It serves the San Francisco Bay Area's Hindu community and is known for its Maha Shivaratri and Navaratri celebrations.

temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple (Balaji Mandir)
temples.about: One of the largest Hindu temples in the United States, dedicated to Lord Venkateswara with shrines to Padmavati, Andal and many others. It serves the large Hindu community of New Jersey and New York and is known for its Brahmotsavam and its daily kalyanotsavam.

temples.name: Sri Ganesha Temple
temples.about: Built in the Chola style with a tall rajagopuram, this temple of Ganesha is a landmark of the American South. It serves Hindu families across Tennessee and is known for its Ganesha Chaturthi and Vinayaka festivals.

temples.name: Kauai's Hindu Monastery (Iraivan Temple)
temples.about: A Shaiva monastery founded in 1970 beside the Wailua River, where the Kadavul temple holds a Nataraja in daily worship and the Iraivan Temple, carved by hand in white granite in India and assembled on the island, is dedicated to Shiva as a crystal lingam.

temples.name: Neem Karoli Baba Ashram and Hanuman Temple
temples.about: An ashram in memory of the saint Neem Karoli Baba, centred on a large murti of Hanuman lying in flight, brought from India in the 1970s. Visitors come for the daily arati, the singing of the Hanuman Chalisa and the meals served to all.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago (Rama Temple)
temples.about: Consecrated in 1986, the temple on the hill at Lemont is dedicated to Rama with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman, beside a Ganesha-Shiva-Durga temple in the North Indian style. It serves the Hindu community of the Chicago area and is known for Ram Navami and Diwali.

temples.name: Durga Temple of Virginia
temples.about: A temple of Ma Durga serving the Washington DC area, with shrines to many deities. It is known for its Navaratri festival, when devotees gather each night for puja, garba and bhajans.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Atlanta (Sri Venkateswara)
temples.about: A temple of Sri Venkateswara built in the South Indian style, with a Shiva temple beside it, serving the Hindu community of Georgia. It is known for its Brahmotsavam and its kalyanotsavam.

temples.name: Kali Mandir
temples.about: A small temple of Ma Kali in the hills of Laguna Beach, where worship follows the Bengali tradition of Dakshineswar. It is known for its Kali Puja and Durga Puja, open to all who come.
air: John Wayne Orange County International Airport

temples.name: Hindu Temple and Cultural Center of Birmingham
temples.about: Opened in 1998, the temple serves Hindu families across central Alabama with daily worship, and its cultural center hosts celebrations of festivals such as Diwali.

temples.name: Sri Ganesha Temple of Alaska
temples.about: Alaska's first Hindu temple, founded in 1999 with a murti of Ganesha given by Sivaya Subramuniyaswami; Durga and Rama are also worshipped here. It is often described as the northernmost Hindu temple in the world.

temples.name: Maha Ganapati Temple of Arizona
temples.about: Opened in 2008 in the desert south of Phoenix, a temple of Maha Ganapati in the South Indian style, serving Hindu families across Arizona.

temples.name: HANWA Hindu Temple
temples.about: Opened in 2012, the temple of the Hindu Association of Northwest Arkansas serves the families of Bentonville and the surrounding region.

temples.name: Shiva Vishnu Temple of Little Rock
temples.about: The temple of the Vedanta Society of Arkansas, founded in 1989, with Shiva and Vishnu as its presiding deities, serving the Little Rock area.
air: Bill & Hillary Clinton National Airport/Adams Field

temples.name: Hindu Temple and Cultural Center of the Rockies
temples.about: The community temple of the Denver area, whose services reach Hindu families in Colorado, Wyoming, Utah, New Mexico and neighbouring states.

temples.name: Sri Satyanarayana Temple
temples.about: Opened in May 1999 near Wesleyan University, the temple of Sri Satyanarayana, a form of Vishnu, serves Hindu families across Connecticut.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Delaware (Mahalakshmi Devasthanam)
temples.about: Inaugurated in 2002 as Delaware's first Hindu temple, with Mahalakshmi as its presiding deity. A 25-foot statue of Hanuman, installed in 2020, stands in its grounds.

temples.name: Shiva Vishnu Temple of South Florida
temples.about: A temple of Shiva and Vishnu in the South Indian style, serving the Hindu community of the Miami and Fort Lauderdale area.

temples.name: Boise Hare Krishna Temple
temples.about: The ISKCON temple and Vedic cultural center near Boise State University, dedicated to Krishna; its temple building opened in 1999.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Central Indiana
temples.about: The community temple of Indianapolis, serving Hindu families across central Indiana with daily worship and the major festivals of the year.

temples.name: Hindu Temple and Cultural Center of Iowa
temples.about: The Hindu community temple of Iowa, in the countryside north of Des Moines.

temples.name: Hindu Temple and Cultural Center of Kansas City
temples.about: The community temple of the Kansas City area, serving Hindu families on both sides of the Kansas-Missouri line.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Kentucky
temples.about: Opened in 1999 on about twenty acres of donated land in northeast Jefferson County, the temple of Kentucky's Hindu community.

temples.name: Sri Venkata Satyanarayana Temple
temples.about: The temple of Sri Venkata Satyanarayana, a form of Vishnu, where the community of New Orleans gathers for worship, including the full-moon Satyanarayana puja.
air: Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport

temples.name: Maine Hindu Temple
temples.about: Maine's Hindu temple, opened in 2013 in a former Universalist church in Westbrook; Ganesha festivals and the wedding of Sita and Rama are among its celebrations.

temples.name: Sri Siva Vishnu Temple
temples.about: A large temple with Shiva and Vishnu as its presiding deities, built in the South Indian style and serving the Washington DC area.

temples.name: Murugan Temple of North America
temples.about: A temple of Lord Murugan with Valli and Deivanai, among the first Murugan temples in North America, known for its Skanda Shashti and Thaipusam festivals.

temples.name: Sri Lakshmi Temple
temples.about: The first traditional Hindu temple in New England, dedicated to Mahalakshmi and built in the South Indian style, serving Hindu families across the region.

temples.name: Parashakthi Temple
temples.about: A temple of the Divine Mother as Karumari Amman, Parashakthi, on a hill in Pontiac north of Detroit.

temples.name: Sri Kasi Vishwanatha Temple
temples.about: A temple of Shiva as Kasi Vishwanatha, serving the Hindu community of Flint and mid-Michigan.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Minnesota
temples.about: Completed in 2009, one of the largest Hindu temples in North America, with shrines in both North and South Indian styles, serving Hindus across the Upper Midwest.
air: Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport / Wold–Chamberlain Field

temples.name: Hindu Temple Society of Mississippi
temples.about: Established in 1986, the society's temple east of Jackson was completed by artisans invited from India; its Holi Mela is a highlight of spring.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of St. Louis
temples.about: The community temple of the St. Louis area, with shrines in North and South Indian styles serving Hindu families across eastern Missouri.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Omaha
temples.about: Completed in 2004, the temple of Nebraska's Hindu community, serving the Omaha metro area.

temples.name: Hindu and Jain Temple of Las Vegas
temples.about: A temple shared by the Hindu and Jain communities of Las Vegas, with daily worship and the major festivals of both traditions.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of New Hampshire
temples.about: The Hindu community temple of New Hampshire, in Nashua.

temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple of North Carolina
temples.about: A temple of Lord Venkateswara in the South Indian style, serving the Hindu community of the Raleigh-Durham area.

temples.name: Shiva Vishnu Temple of Greater Cleveland
temples.about: A temple of Shiva and Vishnu in the South Indian style, serving the Hindu community of Greater Cleveland.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Greater Cincinnati
temples.about: Known as Devdham, the community temple of Greater Cincinnati, with shrines to many deities in North and South Indian styles.

temples.name: Oklahoma City Hindu Temple
temples.about: The community temple of Oklahoma City, serving Hindu families across Oklahoma.

temples.name: Portland Hindu Temple (Brahmma Premananda Ashram)
temples.about: A Hindu temple and ashram in the Portland area, serving devotees across Oregon.

temples.name: Rhode Island Hindu Temple
temples.about: The Rhode Island Hindu Temple Society, founded in 2013, bought the former Temple Am David in Warwick in 2016, giving the state its first Hindu temple.
air: Rhode Island T. F. Green International Airport

temples.name: Hindu Temple of South Carolina
temples.about: Completed in 1984, with its murtis installed in 1986, the community temple of South Carolina's capital.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Siouxland
temples.about: Opened in October 2018 just outside Tea near Sioux Falls, the first Hindu temple in the Dakotas.
air: Sioux Gateway Airport / Brigadier General Bud Day Field

temples.name: India Cultural Center and Temple
temples.about: The temple and cultural center of the Memphis Hindu community, with shrines to many deities and a busy calendar of festivals.

temples.name: Sri Meenakshi Temple
temples.about: A temple of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar built in the style of Madurai, serving the Houston area; its towers were carved by sculptors from Tamil Nadu.

temples.name: Karya Siddhi Hanuman Temple
temples.about: A temple of Hanuman in Frisco, north of Dallas, founded under the guidance of Sri Ganapathy Sachchidananda Swamiji and known for its Hanuman Jayanti celebrations.

temples.name: DFW Hindu Temple
temples.about: The Dallas-Fort Worth Hindu Temple Society's temple in Irving, with shrines to many deities, serving the Hindu community of North Texas.

temples.name: Radha Madhav Dham
temples.about: A temple and ashram of Radha Krishna in the hills south-west of Austin, founded by disciples of Jagadguru Shree Kripalu Ji Maharaj.

temples.name: Sri Sri Radha Krishna Temple
temples.about: A temple of Radha Krishna on a hill in the Utah valley, famous for its Festival of Colors, the Holi celebration that draws tens of thousands each spring.

temples.name: Vermont Hindu Temple
temples.about: Established in 2015 by refugee families from Bhutan and Nepal, the community worships together in Burlington.

temples.name: Hindu Temple and Cultural Center
temples.about: The temple of the Seattle area's Hindu community; its shrine, consecrated in 2014, was the first formally consecrated Hindu temple shrine in the Pacific Northwest.
air: King County International Airport - Boeing Field

temples.name: Sri Sri Radha Vrindavan Chandra Temple and Prabhupada's Palace of Gold
temples.place: New Vrindaban, Moundsville, West Virginia, USA
temples.about: In the hills of the New Vrindaban community, ISKCON's temple of Radha Vrindavan Chandra and the Palace of Gold, built by devotees in memory of A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada.
air: Morgantown Municipal Airport Walter L. (Bill) Hart Field

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Wisconsin
temples.about: The community temple of the Milwaukee area, serving Hindu families across Wisconsin.

temples.name: Shri Venkateswara (Balaji) Temple of UK
temples.about: Built on a hillside in the West Midlands, among the largest Hindu temples in Europe, dedicated to Lord Venkateswara in the South Indian style.

temples.name: Bhaktivedanta Manor
temples.about: ISKCON's temple of Radha Krishna in a manor house given by George Harrison in 1973, the movement's UK headquarters. Its Janmashtami festival draws tens of thousands.

temples.name: Shree Ghanapathy Temple
temples.about: Founded by Sri Lankan Saivite families who began worshipping Ganapathy in a local hall in 1979; one of the earliest traditional South Indian temples in Britain.

temples.name: Highgate Hill Murugan Temple
temples.about: A temple of Lord Murugan in north London, built in the South Indian style and a centre of the city's Tamil community.

temples.name: London Sri Murugan Temple
temples.about: A granite temple of Lord Murugan in east London, built by Tamil craftsmen in the Dravidian style.

temples.name: Skanda Vale
temples.about: A monastic community in the Welsh hills founded in 1973 by Guru Sri Subramanium, with temples to Lord Murugan, the Divine Mother and Vishnu, visited by pilgrims of every faith.

temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple
temples.about: Consecrated in 1985 on the edge of the Royal National Park south of Sydney, a heritage-listed temple of Lord Venkateswara in the South Indian style.

temples.name: Sydney Murugan Temple
temples.place: Mays Hill, New South Wales, Australia
temples.about: A temple of Lord Murugan in western Sydney, built in the Dravidian style and a centre of Sydney's Tamil community, known for its Skanda Shashti and chariot festivals.

temples.name: Shri Shiva Vishnu Temple
temples.about: Consecrated in 1994 by the Hindu Society of Victoria, a temple of Shiva and Vishnu south-east of Melbourne with a cultural centre, library and heritage museum.

temples.name: Perth Hindu Temple (Shri Shiva Temple)
temples.about: The oldest Hindu temple in Western Australia; its land was consecrated in 1987 and its murtis installed in 1990.

temples.name: Sri Selva Vinayakar Koyil
temples.about: A temple of Ganesha as Selva Vinayakar in the countryside south of Brisbane, serving Hindu families across Queensland.

temples.name: Shri Ganesha Temple
temples.about: Opened in 2001 by the Hindu Society of South Australia, the state's first traditional Hindu temple, now on the South Australian heritage register.

temples.name: Richmond Hill Hindu Temple
temples.about: The temple of the Hindu Temple Society of Canada, chartered in 1973, a landmark of South Indian temple architecture north of Toronto.

temples.name: Sringeri Temple of Toronto
temples.about: A temple of Sharadamba, Saraswati as worshipped at Sringeri, run by the Sringeri Vidya Bharati Foundation.

temples.name: Sri Mariamman Temple
temples.about: Singapore's oldest Hindu temple, founded in 1827 and a national monument, known for its Theemithi fire-walking festival before Deepavali.

temples.name: Sri Srinivasa Perumal Temple
temples.about: A temple of Vishnu as Srinivasa Perumal on Serangoon Road and a national monument; Singapore's Thaipusam procession begins here.

temples.name: Sri Thendayuthapani Temple
temples.about: The Chettiar community's temple of Murugan on Tank Road, where Singapore's Thaipusam procession ends.

temples.name: Batu Caves (Sri Subramaniar Swamy Temple)
temples.about: The Temple Cave, reached by 272 steps, where K. Thamboosamy Pillai installed the murti of Sri Subramaniar Swamy in 1891. A golden statue of Murugan stands at its foot, and it is the heart of Malaysia's Thaipusam.
air: Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah International Airport

temples.name: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil
temples.about: Jaffna's great temple of Murugan, worshipped in the form of the Vel; its festival in August and September, closing with the chariot and the water-cutting, is the largest in the Tamil north.

temples.name: Koneswaram Temple
temples.about: On Swami Rock above the sea at Trincomalee, one of the Pancha Ishwarams of Lanka, sacred to Shiva and praised in the Thevaram hymns.

temples.name: Munneswaram Temple
temples.about: One of the Pancha Ishwarams of Lanka, an ancient temple of Shiva near Chilaw whose August festival draws Hindu and Buddhist pilgrims alike.

temples.name: Ganga Talao (Grand Bassin)
temples.about: The crater lake in the south of Mauritius, regarded as joined to the Ganges, with temples on its shore and a tall statue of Shiva as Mangal Mahadev at its entrance; the island's Maha Shivaratree pilgrimage walks here.

temples.name: Sri Siva Subramaniya Swami Temple
temples.about: A temple of Murugan in the Dravidian style in Nadi, built by the Then India Sanmarga Ikya Sangam and carved by craftsmen from India.

temples.name: Temple in the Sea
temples.about: Built out into the Gulf of Paria by Sewdass Sadhu, who carried stones into the sea for years after his first temple on land was removed; rebuilt in 1995, it is a place of pilgrimage for Trinidad's Hindus.

temples.name: Sri Sri Radha Radhanath Temple of Understanding
temples.about: ISKCON's temple of Radha Krishna in Chatsworth, opened in 1985, whose lotus-shaped design and gardens are a landmark of Durban.

temples.name: Bharatiya Mandir
temples.about: A community temple in Auckland with shrines to many deities, serving New Zealand's Hindu families.

temples.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
temples.about: Built by Rajaraja Chola I and completed in 1010, the Big Temple's vimana rises over sixty metres. A UNESCO World Heritage Site, it is the high point of Chola architecture and still a living temple of Shiva.

temples.name: Thillai Nataraja Temple
temples.about: Shiva as Nataraja, the cosmic dancer, in the golden hall. It is the Akasha (space) sthalam of the Pancha Bhoota temples, and the Margazhi Arudra Darshan draws devotees from across the Tamil world.

temples.name: Ekambareswarar Temple
temples.about: The Prithvi (earth) sthalam of the Pancha Bhoota temples, with one of the tallest gopurams in South India and an ancient mango tree in its courtyard, where Parvati is said to have worshipped Shiva.

temples.name: Kamakshi Amman Temple
temples.about: The seat of the Goddess as Kamakshi, seated in padmasana. Closely tied to Adi Shankara and the Kanchi math, it is among the most revered Devi temples of the South.

temples.name: Varadaraja Perumal Temple
temples.about: One of the 108 Divya Desams, with its hundred-pillared hall of carvings. Every forty years the ancient wooden image of Athi Varadar is brought out of the temple tank for forty-eight days.

temples.name: Arunachaleswarar Temple
temples.about: The Agni (fire) sthalam, at the foot of the holy Arunachala hill. On Karthigai Deepam a great flame is lit on the summit, and on full moons tens of thousands walk the fourteen-kilometre Girivalam around the hill.
tips: Girivalam, the walk around the hill, is best known on full-moon nights; many walk it barefoot.

temples.name: Jambukeswarar Temple
temples.about: The Appu (water) sthalam, where an underground spring keeps the sanctum's floor wet. It stands on Srirangam island near the Ranganathaswamy temple.

temples.name: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
temples.about: The great temple of Mylapore, with its colourful gopuram and temple tank. Its Panguni festival, with the procession of the sixty-three Nayanmars, fills the streets of old Chennai.

temples.name: Parthasarathy Temple
temples.about: Krishna as Arjuna's charioteer, one of the 108 Divya Desams, sung by the Alvars. The image of Krishna bears the marks of the arrows from the Kurukshetra war.

temples.name: Tiruttani Murugan Temple
temples.about: One of Murugan's Arupadai Veedu, the six abodes, on a hill of 365 steps, one for each day of the year. Here Murugan is said to have rested after the battle with Surapadman and married Valli.

temples.name: Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple
temples.about: The first of the Arupadai Veedu, cut into a rock hill outside Madurai, where Murugan married Deivanai.

temples.name: Samayapuram Mariamman Temple
temples.about: One of the most visited Mariamman temples of Tamil Nadu, near Tiruchirappalli. Its Poochoridal festival covers the Goddess in flowers.

temples.name: Kumari Amman Temple
temples.about: At the southern tip of India, where three seas meet, the Goddess stands as the virgin Kanya Kumari. It is one of the Shakti Peethas, and her diamond nose ring is said to be seen from the sea.

temples.name: Thanumalayan Temple
temples.about: One image honours Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma together as Sthanu-Mal-Ayan. Its musical pillars and towering Hanuman are among the wonders of Kanyakumari district.

temples.name: Nellaiappar Temple
temples.about: Twin temples of Shiva as Nellaiappar and Parvati as Kanthimathi, among the largest in Tamil Nadu, with musical stone pillars in its halls.

temples.name: Sarangapani Temple
temples.about: A Divya Desam in the temple town of Kumbakonam, its sanctum shaped like a chariot drawn by horses and elephants. The town's Mahamaham festival every twelve years draws millions.

temples.name: Chottanikkara Bhagavathy Temple
temples.about: The Goddess worshipped as Saraswati in the morning, Lakshmi at noon and Durga in the evening. The Makam Thozhal in Kumbham is its great day.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Vadakkunnathan Temple
temples.about: The great Shiva temple at the heart of Thrissur, a classic of Kerala architecture with its murals. Its grounds host Thrissur Pooram, the most famous of Kerala's temple festivals.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Ambalappuzha Sri Krishna Temple
temples.about: Famous for its palpayasam, a milk pudding offered to Krishna and shared as prasadam, and for its links to the Chempakassery kings.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Vaikom Mahadeva Temple
temples.about: One of Kerala's great Shiva temples, with the Vaikathashtami festival in Vrischikam. The 1924 Vaikom Satyagraha here was a landmark in opening temple roads to all.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Ettumanoor Mahadeva Temple
temples.about: Known for its Dravidian-Kerala architecture and murals, among them a celebrated painting of Nataraja. Its Ezhara Ponnana festival brings out seven and a half golden elephants.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Thirunelli Maha Vishnu Temple
temples.about: An ancient temple in the forests of the Brahmagiri hills in Wayanad, beside the Papanasini stream, where families come to remember their ancestors.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Kodungallur Bhagavathy Temple
temples.about: One of Kerala's oldest Bhadrakali temples, known for the Bharani festival in Meenam.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Thrikkakara Vamana Temple
temples.about: One of the very few temples of Vishnu as Vamana, and the home of Onam: the ten-day festival here is said to be where the celebration of Mahabali began.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple
temples.about: Krishna as Parthasarathy, beside the Pampa river. The Aranmula Uthrattathi snake-boat race honours the temple each year, and the Thanka Anki procession to Sabarimala sets out from here.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Haripad Subrahmanya Temple
temples.about: One of Kerala's oldest Murugan temples, with a four-armed image of Subrahmanya, central to the town's life and festivals.
tips: Kerala temples keep a traditional dress code: men in mundu, usually without a shirt inside; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.

temples.name: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
temples.about: Founded by Madhvacharya in the thirteenth century. Krishna is seen through a nine-holed window, the Kanakana Kindi, and worship is led by eight mathas in turn under the Paryaya system.

temples.name: Sri Manjunatha Temple
temples.about: Shiva as Manjunatha, in a temple run by a Jain family and served by Madhva priests, known for feeding thousands of pilgrims every day.

temples.name: Kollur Mookambika Temple
temples.about: The Goddess as Mookambika at the foot of the Kodachadri hills, closely tied to Adi Shankara. Children are brought here for Vidyarambham on Vijayadashami.

temples.name: Chamundeshwari Temple
temples.about: On Chamundi Hill above Mysuru, the Goddess who slew Mahishasura. She is the guardian deity of the Mysuru royal family, and the city's Dasara is held in her honour.

temples.name: Mahabaleshwar Temple
temples.about: Home of the Atmalinga, which Ravana is said to have set down here. A coastal pilgrimage town and a centre of Sanskrit learning.

temples.name: Murudeshwar Temple
temples.about: On a headland in the Arabian Sea, with one of the tallest gopurams in the world and a giant Shiva facing the sea.

temples.name: Virupaksha Temple
temples.about: Worshipped without a break since the seventh century, the heart of Vijayanagara's capital, part of the Hampi UNESCO World Heritage Site.

temples.name: Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple
temples.about: Where Ramanujacharya lived for over a decade. Its Vairamudi festival, when the deity wears a diamond crown, draws pilgrims from across the South.

temples.name: Annapoorneshwari Temple
temples.about: The Goddess as the giver of food, in the hills of the Western Ghats; every pilgrim is fed.

temples.name: Ranganathaswamy Temple
temples.about: On an island in the Kaveri, the first of the three great Ranganatha temples along the river, with Srirangam and Shivanasamudra.

temples.name: Banashankari Temple
temples.about: The Goddess of the forest, family deity of many in North Karnataka. Its Banashankari Jatre in Pushya draws huge crowds.

temples.name: Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
temples.about: Vishnu as Varaha and Narasimha together, covered in sandalwood paste all year; the true form is seen only on Akshaya Tritiya, the Chandanotsavam.

temples.name: Srikalahasti Temple
temples.about: The Vayu (air) sthalam of the Pancha Bhoota temples, where a lamp in the sanctum flickers though no breeze can reach it.

temples.name: Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy Temple
temples.about: On the Ratnagiri hill, the most famous place for the Satyanarayana Vratam, performed here by families every day.

temples.name: Ahobilam Narasimha Temples
temples.about: Nine shrines of Narasimha in the Nallamala hills, where Narasimha is said to have appeared to protect Prahlada; a Divya Desam.

temples.name: Panakala Narasimha Temple
temples.about: Narasimha on the hill takes jaggery water, panakam, as his offering; half of what is poured in is said to be returned as prasadam.

temples.name: Arasavalli Sun Temple
temples.about: One of the few living temples of Surya in India. On Ratha Saptami and at the equinoxes the first rays of the sun fall on the deity's feet.

temples.name: Bhimeswara Swamy Temple
temples.about: One of the five Pancharama shrines of Shiva, and a Shakti Peetha of Manikyamba.

temples.name: Dwaraka Tirumala
temples.about: Venkateswara on a hill in West Godavari, called the Chinna Tirupati, the smaller Tirupati, by the many who visit.

temples.name: Veerabhadra Temple
temples.about: A Vijayanagara temple with a famous hanging pillar, ceiling murals and a monolithic Nandi, one of the largest in India.

temples.name: Mahanandi Temple
temples.about: In the Nallamala forest, with crystal-clear spring pools fed all year, the centre of the nine Nandi shrines of the region.

temples.name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
temples.about: Narasimha in a cave shrine on Yadadri hill, rebuilt in black granite as one of the grandest temples of Telangana.

temples.name: Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple
temples.about: On the Godavari, built by Bhakta Ramadas, whose songs are still sung across the Telugu land. The celestial wedding of Rama and Sita on Sri Rama Navami is its great day.

temples.name: Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Temple
temples.about: One of the most visited Shiva temples of Telangana, known as Dakshina Kashi.

temples.name: Gnana Saraswati Temple
temples.about: One of the few great temples of Saraswati, on the Godavari. Children are brought here for Aksharabhyasam, their first letters.

temples.name: Chilkur Balaji Temple
temples.about: The visa Balaji, an old temple of Venkateswara outside Hyderabad, known for accepting no money: there is no hundi and no paid darshan.

temples.name: Ramappa Temple
temples.about: A Kakatiya temple of the thirteenth century, named after its sculptor, with bracket figures of dancers; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

temples.name: Thousand Pillar Temple
temples.about: A Kakatiya temple of Shiva, Vishnu and Surya, with a star-shaped plan and a great hall of carved pillars.

temples.name: Jogulamba Temple
temples.about: A Shakti Peetha on the Tungabhadra, beside the Navabrahma temples of the Badami Chalukyas.

temples.name: Ujjaini Mahankali Temple
temples.about: In Secunderabad, the centre of the Bonalu festival in Ashadha, when women carry pots of rice to the Goddess.

temples.name: Birla Mandir
temples.about: A white-marble temple of Venkateswara on Naubat Pahad above Hussain Sagar, built in 1976.

temples.name: Manakula Vinayagar Temple
temples.about: Ganesha in the old French quarter of Puducherry, older than the French settlement, with a temple elephant who blesses visitors.

temples.name: Shri Mangueshi Temple
temples.about: The family deity of many Goan Saraswat families, Shiva as Mangesh, with its seven-storey lamp tower.

temples.name: Shri Shantadurga Temple
temples.about: The Goddess as peacemaker between Shiva and Vishnu, in one of Goa's largest temples.

temples.name: Shri Mahalasa Narayani Temple
temples.about: The Goddess as Mohini, Vishnu's enchanting form, family deity of many Konkani families.

temples.name: Shri Saptakoteshwar Temple
temples.about: Rebuilt by Chhatrapati Shivaji in 1668, a symbol of Goan Hindu continuity.

temples.name: Bhimashankar Temple
temples.about: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, in the forests of the Sahyadri, at the source of the Bhima river.

temples.name: Grishneshwar Temple
temples.about: The last of the twelve Jyotirlingas, beside the Ellora caves, rebuilt in red stone by Ahilyabai Holkar.

temples.name: Aundha Nagnath Temple
temples.about: Counted by many among the twelve Jyotirlingas, an ancient stone temple in Hingoli district.

temples.name: Vaidyanath Temple
temples.about: Counted by many in Maharashtra as a Jyotirlinga, its temple restored by Ahilyabai Holkar.

temples.name: Tulja Bhavani Temple
temples.about: The Goddess Bhavani, family deity of Chhatrapati Shivaji and countless Maharashtrian families, one of the Shakti Peethas of Maharashtra.

temples.name: Saptashrungi Devi Temple
temples.about: The eighteen-armed Goddess on a peak of seven summits near Nashik, counted as the half of Maharashtra's three and a half Shakti Peethas.

temples.name: Mahalakshmi Temple
temples.about: On the sea at Breach Candy, the Goddess as Mahalakshmi with Mahakali and Mahasaraswati; Mumbai's busiest temple at Navratri.

temples.name: Mayureshwar Temple
temples.about: The first and most important of the Ashtavinayak, the eight Ganesha temples around Pune.

temples.name: Khandoba Temple
temples.about: Khandoba, the warrior form of Shiva and family deity of many in the Deccan, where devotees shower turmeric on the hill.

temples.name: Swayambhu Ganpati Temple
temples.about: Ganesha in a natural rock form on the Konkan shore, facing west to the sea.

temples.name: Dwarkadhish Temple
temples.about: Krishna as king of Dwarka, one of the four Char Dham, its flag changed several times a day above the Gomti.

temples.name: Nageshwar Jyotirlinga
temples.about: Counted among the twelve Jyotirlingas, near Dwarka, with a tall seated Shiva outside.

temples.name: Ambaji Temple
temples.about: A Shakti Peetha where the Goddess is worshipped through the sacred Visa Yantra, with no image; the Bhadarvi Poonam fair draws millions.

temples.name: Kalika Mata Temple
temples.about: On the Pavagadh hill, part of the Champaner-Pavagadh UNESCO site, a Shakti Peetha of Kali.

temples.name: Ranchhodraiji Temple
temples.about: Krishna as Ranchhodrai, said to have come from Dwarka with his devotee Bodana; the Sharad Purnima fair is its great day.

temples.name: Shamlaji Temple
temples.about: An ancient Vishnu temple in the Aravalli foothills, beloved of the Bhil communities of the region.

temples.name: Swaminarayan Akshardham
temples.about: A pink sandstone monument to Bhagwan Swaminarayan, with exhibitions on Hindu culture and gardens.

temples.name: Bahuchara Mata Temple
temples.about: The Goddess Bahuchara, one of Gujarat's three Shakti Peethas with Ambaji and Pavagadh.

temples.name: Kashtbhanjan Hanuman Temple
temples.about: A Swaminarayan temple of Hanuman, among the most visited in Gujarat.

temples.name: Chamunda Mata Temple
temples.about: The Goddess Chamunda on a hilltop reached by a long flight of steps in Saurashtra.

temples.name: Jagatpita Brahma Temple
temples.about: One of very few temples of Brahma in the world, beside the sacred Pushkar lake; the Kartik Purnima fair is its great day.

temples.name: Shrinathji Temple
temples.about: Krishna as the child Shrinathji lifting Govardhan, centre of the Pushtimarg tradition, with its eight darshans a day and pichwai paintings.

temples.name: Khatu Shyam Temple
temples.about: Barbarika, worshipped as Shyam, a form of Krishna; his Phalgun fair draws millions.

temples.name: Mehandipur Balaji Temple
temples.about: Hanuman as Balaji, with Pretraj and Bhairav, among the most visited temples of Rajasthan.
air: Agra Airport / Agra Air Force Station

temples.name: Karni Mata Temple
temples.about: The temple of the warrior-sage Karni Mata near Bikaner, famous for the thousands of rats that live there and are held sacred.

temples.name: Eklingji Temple
temples.about: Shiva as Ekling, the true ruler of Mewar in whose name the Maharanas governed.

temples.name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
temples.about: Krishna in the City Palace grounds, the guardian of Jaipur; its aartis fill the courtyard each day.

temples.name: Birla Mandir
temples.about: A white-marble Lakshmi Narayan temple below Moti Dungri, built in 1988.

temples.name: Galtaji Temple
temples.about: Temples and natural spring tanks in a gorge outside Jaipur, a centre of the Ramanandi tradition.

temples.name: Tanot Mata Temple
temples.about: Near the border in the Thar desert, the Goddess revered by soldiers, cared for by the Border Security Force.
air: Begum Nusrat Bhutto International Airport Sukkur

temples.name: Omkareshwar Temple
temples.about: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, on an island in the Narmada shaped like the sacred syllable Om.
air: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar International Airport

temples.name: Harsiddhi Temple
temples.about: A Shakti Peetha beside Mahakaleshwar, with two great lamp towers lit at Navratri.
air: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar International Airport

temples.name: Kal Bhairav Temple
temples.about: Bhairava, the guardian of Ujjain, an ancient temple on the Shipra.
air: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar International Airport

temples.name: Chintaman Ganesh Temple
temples.about: An ancient Ganesha temple outside Ujjain, with Ganesha worshipped in three forms.
air: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar International Airport

temples.name: Ram Raja Temple
temples.about: The only temple where Rama is worshipped as a king, given a guard of honour each day.

temples.name: Maa Sharda Temple
temples.about: The Goddess Sharda on Trikuta hill, reached by over a thousand steps or a ropeway.

temples.name: Matangeshwar Temple
temples.about: The one temple of the Khajuraho group still in daily worship, with a great lingam over two and a half metres high.

temples.name: Narmada Udgam Temple
temples.about: Where the Narmada rises, a temple town of the Maikal hills revered as the river's birthplace.

temples.name: Pitambara Peeth
temples.about: A centre of worship of the Goddess Baglamukhi and Dhumavati.
air: Agra Airport / Agra Air Force Station

temples.name: Bhojeshwar Temple
temples.about: An unfinished eleventh-century temple of Raja Bhoj with one of the largest lingams in India.
air: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar International Airport

temples.name: Danteshwari Temple
temples.about: The guardian Goddess of Bastar, at the meeting of two rivers; the Bastar Dussehra honours her for seventy-five days.

temples.name: Mahamaya Temple
temples.about: The Goddess Mahamaya in the old capital of the Kalachuris, a centre of Navratri worship.

temples.name: Maa Bamleshwari Temple
temples.about: The Goddess Bamleshwari on a 1,600-foot hill, its Navratri fairs drawing pilgrims from across central India.

temples.name: Rajiv Lochan Temple
temples.about: At the meeting of three rivers, the Prayag of Chhattisgarh, with its Rajim Kumbh in Magha.

temples.name: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple
temples.about: At Rama's birthplace in Ayodhya, consecrated in 2024 in the Nagara style; Ram Navami is its great festival.
tips: Phones, bags and footwear are left at the free counters before entry; carry an ID.

temples.name: Shri Krishna Janmasthan Temple
temples.about: Built at the place revered as Krishna's birthplace; Janmashtami midnight here is kept by vast crowds.
air: Agra Airport / Agra Air Force Station

temples.name: Banke Bihari Temple
temples.about: Krishna as Banke Bihari, whose curtain is drawn every few moments; Vrindavan's most visited temple, alive at Holi and Janmashtami.
air: Agra Airport / Agra Air Force Station

temples.name: Prem Mandir
temples.about: A white Italian-marble temple of Radha Krishna and Sita Rama, lit in changing colours each evening.
air: Agra Airport / Agra Air Force Station

temples.name: Krishna Balaram Mandir
temples.about: The ISKCON temple founded by Srila Prabhupada, with Krishna and Balarama and constant kirtan.
air: Agra Airport / Agra Air Force Station

temples.name: Dwarkadhish Temple
temples.about: A temple of Krishna as Dwarkadhish near the Vishram Ghat, famous for its swing festival in Shravan.
air: Agra Airport / Agra Air Force Station

temples.name: Vishalakshi Temple
temples.about: A Shakti Peetha near Manikarnika ghat, the Goddess as Vishalakshi, of the wide eyes.
